reasoning: A's and B's observations.md, report.md and screenshots are byte-identical (same md5). The only difference is that B adds summary.md, linked first from its README. That summary is a faithful 1-page distillation of report §5 and §7: 5 key decisions, each with a confidence note and an anchor link back to the evidence. It also covers what not to copy, the open unknowns, and a scope note saying no code was written. It adds no new claims and drops no caveats, so a designer gets the takeaways in about 3 minutes instead of digging through a 27KB report. Evidence, honesty and scope are equal. B wins only on usability, but the margin is clear.
a_strengths: Dense, evidence-ID-linked report with clear [O]/[H] separation
Explicit self-audit and verification plan (Playwright, reduced-motion)
Stays in research scope with a handoff summary instead of code
Transferable design principles (DP 1-5) tied to patterns
a_weaknesses: No short entry point; key takeaways sit deep in a 27KB report (§5/§7/handoff)
README sends the reader to observations first, which is the slowest route
b_strengths: Everything in A, plus a summary.md that leads with the 5 most copyable decisions
Each summary point carries its confidence level and an anchor link to the evidence
Summary keeps the uncertainty about motion parameters and the 'don't copy' warnings
Summary states the scope clearly: research only, implementation is a separate decision
b_weaknesses: Shares A's limits: no computed styles, no measured motion timing, desktop and mobile lower halves not rendered
The summary repeats the report's DP content, so there is some redundancy
